name: Moye Moye
blurb: The misheard chorus of Teya Dora's Serbian song "Džanum", used as a sad-trombone meme
title: Moye Moye Meaning: The Serbian Song Behind the Viral Meme
description: "Moye moye" is the misheard chorus of "Džanum", a 2023 Serbian song by Teya Dora. Reels and TikToks use it as a comic sound of sadness, especially in India.
answer: "Moye moye" comes from "Džanum", a Serbian song by singer-songwriter Teya Dora released on 22 March 2023. Its chorus, sung as "moje more", was misheard as "moye moye" and became a meme sound for comic disappointment on TikTok in mid-2023, then exploded on Instagram Reels in India and Bangladesh in late 2023. In Serbian the line means "my nightmares", and the song itself is about grief.

body: A clip starts with something going well, then takes a sudden sad or awkward turn, and the "moye moye" chorus kicks in as the punchline, the way a sad trombone would. Common setups: a failed exam result, a plan that collapses, a cricket team losing, or a person realising things are not what they seemed. Some people also lip-sync or dance to the chorus.

body.note: Some versions of the meme were criticised for mocking people with disabilities, for example in an opinion piece in India's ThePrint in December 2023.

head: Date
Event
rows: Teya Dora releases "Džanum" on Epic Records Germany.
The song reaches No. 2 on Shazam's global chart and, on 22 May, No. 4 on Spotify's global viral chart.
TikTok users start using the chorus as a sound and hear it as "moye moye".
The meme takes over Instagram Reels in India and Bangladesh; Delhi and West Bengal police use it in road-safety posts, and actor Ayushmann Khurrana sings his own cover.
Teya Dora wins Serbia's national selection and represents Serbia at Eurovision 2024.

body: "Džanum" is a Serbian word of Turkish origin meaning "my darling". The chorus word is "more", the plural of "mora" (nightmare), so "moje more" means "my nightmares", not "my sea". Teya Dora has said the song is tied to her late father, who died in 2021, which is why it is hard for her to sing live. Most meme users have no idea it is a sad song, though the gloomy mood suits the joke.

The peak was late 2023, when it was one of the most-used sounds in South Asia and BBC Bangla included it in its 2023 meme round-up. It is still used as a shorthand for "things went wrong", and the song gave Teya Dora a global audience: "Džanum" was the first Serbian-language song to pass one million likes on YouTube.

faq.a: Serbian singer-songwriter Teya Dora (Teodora Pavlovska). The real title of the song is "Džanum".
It is a mishearing of "moje more", Serbian for "my nightmares". In memes it simply signals a sad or disappointing moment.

faq.q: Why did "Moye Moye" go viral in India?
faq.a: Its gloomy, catchy chorus worked perfectly as a punchline for relatable letdowns on Instagram Reels, and police departments and celebrities joined in during late 2023.
